hypothesis: Broadcom offers a lower current cash-flow valuation hurdle than NVIDIA despite its faster AI semiconductor growth, so rotating part of an NVIDIA allocation into Broadcom improves valuation margin of safety.

decision_rule.use_or_condition_if: AVGO must be no more expensive than NVDA on both TTM enterprise-value/free-cash-flow and five-year reverse-DCF implied free-cash-flow growth across the stated sensitivity grid.
decision_rule.reject_if: AVGO requires a higher valuation multiple or higher implied five-year free-cash-flow growth than NVDA under the same assumptions.

verdict_scope: Reject the claim that AVGO is currently the cheaper cash-flow allocation alternative to NVDA. This does not reject AVGO as an AI semiconductor holding or claim that NVDA has the higher future return.

primary_fundamental_sources.document: Q2 FY2027 earnings release and Form 10-Q for quarter ended 2026-07-26
Q3 FY2026 earnings release / Form 8-K exhibit for quarter ended 2026-08-02

NVDA.ttm_fcf_construction: FY2026 FCF 96.575 - first-half FY2026 FCF 39.584 + first-half FY2027 FCF 69.895

AVGO.shares_identity: Q3 FY2026 GAAP diluted weighted-average shares; used as the available primary-source equity-count proxy, not represented as period-end shares outstanding
AVGO.ttm_fcf_construction: Q4 FY2025 FCF 7.466 + first-three-quarters FY2026 FCF 31.937

benchmark.name: simple TTM EV/FCF
benchmark.result: AVGO trades at the higher cash-flow multiple by about 4.0 percent.

reverse_dcf.method: Solve one constant annual FCF growth rate for years 1-5 such that discounted five-year FCF plus year-5 terminal value equals current enterprise value. Terminal value equals year-5 FCF times a terminal EV/FCF multiple.
reverse_dcf.sensitivity_result: AVGO requires the higher five-year FCF CAGR in all 9 of 9 discount-rate and terminal-multiple combinations.

alternative_hypothesis.statement: AVGO's faster current operating growth can still justify the higher valuation hurdle.
alternative_hypothesis.evidence: Latest quarterly FCF grew about 94.5% year over year at AVGO versus about 58.7% at NVDA, while AVGO Q3 AI semiconductor revenue grew 221% year over year. This supports growth strength but does not itself establish a higher future shareholder return because the valuation hurdle is also higher.
alternative_hypothesis.decision: CONDITION only; requires forward, point-in-time FCF realization versus the reverse-DCF hurdle before changing portfolio weights.

risk_and_limitations: This is valuation research, not a historical trading strategy; Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown and Expected Shortfall are not decision-valid outputs for this test.

AVGO market capitalization uses Q3 diluted weighted-average shares as a primary-source proxy because a period-end share count was not verified in this run. The resulting valuation comparison must not be presented as exact to the last basis point.
NVIDIA marketable equity securities are excluded from cash-like assets in enterprise value; only cash and marketable debt securities are netted against debt.
Free-cash-flow definitions are issuer-reported and may differ in detail between companies.
Reverse DCF results are assumption sensitivities, not price targets.

implementation.reason: The cheaper-AVGO thesis was rejected; retain only reusable negative evidence and do not add a production allocation model.

next_high_value_hypothesis: Using point-in-time quarterly FCF through FY2027 and current prices at each rebalance date, does an allocation rule that buys the lower reverse-DCF hurdle between NVDA and AVGO improve cost-adjusted out-of-sample return, maximum drawdown and Expected Shortfall versus NVDA-only and equal-weight NVDA/AVGO?
